exercises.title: Focus Block Roll-up
exercises.prompt: A study timer records consecutive focus blocks as objects with a label and a positive number of minutes. Adjacent blocks with the same label belong to one uninterrupted activity. Return a new list in which adjacent blocks with equal labels are combined by adding their minutes. Blocks with the same label that are separated by another label must remain separate, and the input must not be modified.
constraints: 0 <= blocks.length <= 10000
Each block has a non-empty string label and an integer minutes value from 1 to 1440
Labels are case-sensitive

examples.explanation: Only the first two code blocks are adjacent, so the last code block starts a new group.
An empty timeline has no groups.

exercises.title: Steady Sensor Windows
exercises.prompt: A lab sensor emits an integer reading every minute. A window is steady when the difference between its largest and smallest reading is no greater than maxSpread. Return the zero-based starting index of every steady window containing exactly width readings, in ascending order. Windows may overlap.
constraints: 1 <= readings.length <= 20000
1 <= width <= readings.length
0 <= maxSpread <= 1000000
Each reading is an integer between -1000000 and 1000000

examples.explanation: Readings [4,5,4] and [9,8,9] each have a spread of one.
Every one-reading window has a spread of zero.

exercises.title: Review Wave Planner
exercises.prompt: A release has named review tasks and dependency pairs. Each pair [before, after] means before must finish before after can start. Plan the work as simultaneous waves: every unfinished task whose dependencies are complete belongs to the next wave. Sort task names within each wave. Return all waves, or return an empty list when the dependencies contain a cycle. Tasks without dependencies still belong to the plan.
constraints: 0 <= tasks.length <= 5000
Task names are distinct non-empty strings
Every dependency names two tasks from tasks
A dependency pair contains two different task names

examples.explanation: API and docs can start together; release waits for both its direct and indirect prerequisites.
The two tasks depend on each other, so no valid wave exists.

exercises.title: Workshop Seat Allocation
exercises.prompt: Process workshop seat requests in order. Each request has a team name and a positive seat count. Accept a team's first request only when all requested seats remain, then subtract those seats. Reject every later request from a team that has already appeared, even if its first request was rejected. Other requests that do not fit are rejected for insufficient seats. Return accepted team names, rejected entries with their reason, and the seats remaining.
constraints: 0 <= capacity <= 1000000
0 <= requests.length <= 10000
Each team is a non-empty case-sensitive string
Each seats value is an integer from 1 to 1000000
Rejection reasons must be duplicate-team or insufficient-seats

examples.explanation: Lin's first request is remembered even though it could not be filled; Jo can use the two remaining seats.

exercises.title: Coverage Gap Finder
exercises.prompt: A support day covers the half-open interval [dayStart, dayEnd). Each staffed shift is another half-open interval [start, end). Clip shifts to the support day, combine overlapping or touching coverage, and return every uncovered half-open interval in chronological order. Ignore shifts that do not overlap the support day. Do not modify the shifts input.
constraints: dayStart and dayEnd are integers with dayStart < dayEnd
0 <= shifts.length <= 10000
Every shift contains integer start and end values with start < end
Input shifts may be unsorted and may extend beyond the support day

examples.explanation: The first two shifts overlap and form one coverage interval from 3 to 10.
Neither shift overlaps the half-open support day.

template is a string

0 <= links.length <= 10000
Every link contains two distinct service numbers in the valid range
start and target are valid service numbers

exercises.title: Message Frequency Leaders
exercises.prompt: A message stream is represented by a list of case-sensitive labels. Count every label and return one object for each label whose count is at least threshold. 1 <= threshold <= 20000
Labels are compared case-sensitively

For every node i greater than 0, 0 <= parents[i] < i

exercises.prompt: A coaching organisation is a rooted tree stored as a parent array, with node 0 at the root and every later node attached to an earlier node. Each node has a signed score. parents[0] is -1; for every i greater than 0, 0 <= parents[i] < i
Each score is an integer from -1000 to 1000
0 <= queries.length <= 5000 and every queried node index is valid

exercises.prompt: A compact message was formed by joining registered command tokens without separators. Recover a token sequence that reproduces the whole message using the fewest tokens. Tokens are distinct strings of 1 to 20 lowercase ASCII letters or digits
The message contains only lowercase ASCII letters or digits
Tokens may be reused any number of times

examples.explanation: Both a+bc and ab+c use two tokens, and [a,bc] is lexicographically smaller.

Every link names two different valid node indices; duplicate endpoint pairs are allowed
Every proposal cost is an integer from 1 to 1000000
